inspiration: RE-friction challenge 661daf77cddae72ae250c836; the existing foldcallret single-use contract
decisions: The hypothesis is upheld: foldcallret made a direct call output implied after seeing its single SUBPIECE consumer, while the derived low-word value fanned out and recursively printed the call at both sinks.

The first cross-block-only guard was rejected because a same-block two-sink minimizer still duplicated helper2(). The shipped repair is independent of CFG topology and enforces single evaluation at every multi-use printable root.
This repairs the existing foldcallret contract and adds no option. Option-off was a diagnostic control, not an acceptable fix, because it removes safe single-use folding covered by DIV-14.

The expanded sweep compared 175 in-repo fixtures and 281 RE-dataset paths with 60-second outer and 5-second per-function bounds. All 259 comparable changed functions are materializations; 324 duplicate textual call occurrences disappear, every affected callee remains, and no new callee appears. Thirty-four timeout/error asymmetries are recorded as incomparable, not improvements.

The repaired arm was rebuilt and rerun over all 456 paths after rebasing onto 0f22749d. Every previously comparable JSON result was byte-identical after serially resolving timeout-boundary cases, so the rebase introduced no newly changed function.

The three existing foldcallret catalog prose fields and the two legacy CALLEESCRATCHBODY assertion names remain byte-for-byte unchanged. The stage assertions strengthen only their regex bodies, generated catalog artifacts match origin/main, and mergecheck is clean with zero rejects.
